title: A stale machine pre-triage mark skips the person on a demoted slice
body:
## Summary
A card's `pretriaged_by = machine:dowser` is never cleared, so when the card resurfaces in a later run `pretriageRun` reports it pre-triaged again without checking the slice's current level - even after the slice was demoted to L0.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:198 `if (r.pretriaged_by === MACHINE_DECIDER) { pretriaged.push(item); continue; }` runs before the level check at skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:199.
- The mark is written once at skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:189 (`... AND pretriaged_by IS NULL`) and no code path resets it: the only writers of the column in skill/ are skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:189 and skill/scripts/lib/hydrate.mjs:23 (copy from Forge).
- skill/scripts/lib/triage.mjs:34 `const person = all.filter((r) => r.pretriaged_by !== MACHINE)` then removes the card from the person's pre-triage list, and the push carries the mark into the inbox.
- The contract (docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:60) puts the gate in the store: it 'refuses a machine decision above' the slice's level.

## Flow
- Run 1: slice technical|doc-drift|-|S at L1; card A predicted accept is marked machine:dowser.
- A person rejects another machine-marked card B -> reversal -> slice drops to L0.
- A person snoozes A; A resurfaces in run 2 with new evidence (snoozed -> candidate -> verified).
- pretriage --run run2: A is listed under `pretriaged` with `level: 0`; the person never pre-triages it.

## Expected impact
The demotion that exists to put the person back in the loop is bypassed for exactly the cards that were machine-handled before. Fix: clear `pretriaged_by` when a card leaves `verified/pushed` for `candidate` (resurface) or re-evaluate the level at line 198 for any card whose last_run_id is this run.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the L1 gate holds on a demoted slice.
Before: probe returns pretriaged [{fp: 152582c2054ffec4, slice: technical|doc-drift|-|S, level: 0}], for_person [].
After: the same card lands in for_person at level 0 (a re-check of the level, or a cleared mark on resurface).
Method: probe - a scratch script outside the repo drove the real store (propose, move, allocateRun, pretriageRun) through the flow above; the fix itself was not built (ideas-only).
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: Probe output: `level now 0` then `run2 pretriage {"pretriaged":[{"fp":"152582c2054ffec4","slice":"technical|doc-drift|-|S","level":0}],"for_person":[]}`; skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:198 `if (r.pretriaged_by === MACHINE_DECIDER) { pretriaged.push(item); continue; }`; skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:189 `UPDATE proposals SET pretriaged_by = ? WHERE fp = ? AND status = 'verified' AND pretriaged_by IS NULL`; grep for a statement setting pretriaged_by to NULL over skill/ and forge/src: 0 hits.
impact_why: The trust gate's demotion is bypassed for resurfaced cards: a level-0 slice still skips the person's pre-triage.

title: Trust window counts decision transitions, not decided items
body:
## Summary
The earn window is meant to be 'the last 20 human-decided items' (docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:71-72) but trust.mjs counts every human transition to accepted/rejected/snoozed, so one card that is snoozed, resurfaces and is accepted fills two of the 20 slots, once as a disagreement and once as an agreement.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:46-56 `decisions()` selects `FROM transitions t JOIN proposals p ... WHERE t.to_status IN ('accepted','rejected','snoozed')` - one row per transition, not per fp.
- skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:66-68 `windowStats` slices the last WINDOW of that list.
- skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:85-90 makes repeated decisions on one fp ordinary: pushed -> snoozed -> verified/candidate -> ... -> accepted, and rejected -> candidate -> ... -> rejected.
- Contract: 'agree with the human verdicts on >= 90 % of its last 20 human-decided items (min 20...)'.

## Flow
- Card A predicted accept; a person snoozes it (defer, disagrees), it resurfaces, a person accepts it (agrees).
- trustReport: n = 2, agreement = 0.5 for that slice, from one item.
- A slice of 12 items with 8 snooze-then-accept cycles reaches n = 20 with 60 % agreement - neither the min-20 nor the agreement matches the contract's meaning.

## Expected impact
The earn rule reaches 'min 20' early on churny slices and its agreement mixes intermediate snoozes with final verdicts. Fix: per slice keep the latest human decision per fp in the window (and keep the reversal check per transition).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the window measures what the contract names.
Before: one card, two decisions -> slice n = 2, agreement 0.5 (probe).
After: n = 1, agreement 1.0 (the latest decision of that item).
Method: probe - scratch script drove the real store: snooze, resurface, accept one predicted-accept card, then trustReport; the per-item fix was walked, not built.
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: Probe: `after accept [{"slice":"technical|doc-drift|-|S","level":0,..."n":2,"agreement":0.5}]` with transitions for fp 152582c2054ffec4: `{id:6,to_status:snoozed,by:human:owner}`, `{id:9,to_status:accepted,by:human:owner}`; skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:47-50 `SELECT t.id, t.fp, t.to_status ... FROM transitions t JOIN proposals p ON p.fp = t.fp WHERE t.to_status IN ('accepted', 'rejected', 'snoozed')`; contract docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:71-72 `>= 90 % of its last 20 human-decided items (min 20; ...)`.
impact_why: The earn gate's n and agreement are measured over transitions; churny slices earn or fail L1 on the wrong evidence.

title: Wire check accepts a score its own breakdown does not produce
body:
## Summary
The shared wire validation (skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs, copied to forge/src/shared/model.mjs) checks only that `score` is in (0, 100] and that `score_parts` has five numeric/string keys. It accepts any `formula` string and a score that its own breakdown, and the record's own impact, cannot produce. The Forge inbox sorts on that number (forge/src/core/cards.mjs:198), so one bad producer outranks every honest card.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:523 `if (o.score !== undefined && !(typeof o.score === 'number' && ... o.score > 0 && o.score <= 100))` - the only score check.
- skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:530 `if (!str(sp.formula)) return 'score_parts.formula:required';` - any string passes; docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:36 says a formula change 'is scan-score/2, never an edit', which only helps if a consumer can tell the two apart.
- No check ties score_parts.impact to the record's impact, or score to round1(10*impact*confidence_w/effort_div*risk_factor).
- forge/src/core/cards.mjs:198 `... CASE WHEN score IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, score DESC` - the inbox order.

## Flow
- A record with impact 2, confidence high, size S (scan-score/1 = 12.8) arrives with score 95 and score_parts {impact: 9, confidence_w: 7, effort_div: 0.1, risk_factor: 3, formula: 'made-up'}.
- validateCandidate(wire) -> ok; Forge stores it; the inbox lists it first.
- With the check: refused `score_parts.formula:must be scan-score/1` / `score:does not match score_parts`.

## Expected impact
The contract's 'stored by the producer; consumers sort by it' only holds if the store refuses an inconsistent number. Fix: require formula === FORMULA, score_parts.impact === impact, and score === round1 of the parts (verifying the stored breakdown, not re-ranking), in the shared computedProblem so both sides gain it via sync-shared.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - an inconsistent score cannot reach the inbox order.
Before: probe - validateCandidate({...card, impact 2, score 95, score_parts formula 'made-up', confidence_w 7}, {wire: true}) -> ok:true.
After: the same record is refused; the four contract reference values and every honest record still pass (scanScore of their own parts reproduces them).
Method: probe - ran the shared validateCandidate from a scratch command; the added check was simulated on the reference values.
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: Probe: `made-up {"ok":true,"value":{...}}` for score 95 with score_parts {impact:9, confidence_w:7, effort_div:0.1, risk_factor:3, formula:'made-up'} on an impact-2 card. skill/scripts/lib/model.mjs:530 `if (!str(sp.formula)) return 'score_parts.formula:required';`; forge/src/core/cards.mjs:198 `CASE WHEN score IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, score DESC`.
impact_why: A wrong or foreign-formula score is stored and leads the inbox order; the contract's formula versioning is unenforced.
predicted_why: no precedent (door unreachable, digest absent); contract says consumers never recompute, so verifying the breakdown is a contract call

title: Trust lose rule ignores a snoozed machine pre-triage and L0 reversals
body:
## Summary
The contract drops a slice one level and resets its window 'on any human reversal of a machine decision' (docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:73-74). trust.mjs counts only a rejection as a reversal, so a person snoozing a card the machine pre-triaged as accept is not one; and a reversal while the slice is already at L0 resets nothing, so the next earn window still contains it.

## Description
- skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:55 `reversal: r.pretriaged_by === MACHINE_DECIDER && r.to_status === 'rejected'` - snoozed (defer) is excluded.
- skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:106 `if (d.reversal && level > 0)` - at level 0 neither the level nor `window_after` changes.
- skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:11-12 (header) states the narrower rule ('when a person rejects a card the machine pre-triaged'), so the code matches its own comment but not the contract it cites.
- predict.mjs DECIDED maps snoozed to `defer` (skill/scripts/lib/predict.mjs:25): the machine said accept, the person said defer.

## Flow
- L1 slice marks card A (accept). In Jira the person snoozes A. syncTrust: no level change; A counts only as one disagreement in 20.
- Two machine-marked cards B, C are rejected: B drops the slice to L0 and resets the window; C (level 0) leaves the window open, so C's disagreement stays in the next earn window.

## Expected impact
The lose rule is softer than the contract on the one ladder Dowser has. Fix: treat any human decision other than the predicted verdict on a machine-marked card as a reversal, and reset `window_after` on a reversal even at L0 (or record in the contract that Dowser's reversal is reject-only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the store's lose rule matches scan-finding/1.
Before: the probe flow (stale-mark script) showed a machine-marked card snoozed by human:owner with no trust event; only the rejection of another card produced `reversal: ... rejected`.
After: the snooze also yields a reversal event, and a second reversal at L0 moves window_after.
Method: simulation - walked three cases (snooze at L1, reject at L1, reject at L0) through trust.mjs:96-112; the snooze case was observed in the probe, the L0 case read only.
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:55 `reversal: r.pretriaged_by === MACHINE_DECIDER && r.to_status === 'rejected',`; skill/scripts/lib/trust.mjs:106 `if (d.reversal && level > 0) {`; docs/contracts/scan-finding-1.md:73 `- **Lose:** a slice drops one level, and its window resets, on any human reversal of a machine decision`.
impact_why: The trust gate demotes less often than the contract requires; deferrals of machine accepts never cost the slice its level.
predicted_why: no precedent (door unreachable, digest absent); whether a snooze reverses an accept is a policy call
